A recurring failure mode in this document has been rating-inflation that conflates "code exists and unit tests pass" with "the pipeline runs end-to-end against real substrates." The 2026-04-24 correction pass walked the overall rating back from a self-assessed 9.2 to 8.3 for exactly this reason. Going forward, every status is one of these five terms — never a bare check / warning / cross glyph:
— specified (and possibly schema'd), but no implementation exists yet.

— implemented and unit/property-tested in-tree, but exercised only against stubs / simulators / injected transports / single-process round-trips. Code is present; the system has not been proven against a real external substrate.
— the code path has been exercised end-to-end against its real substrate at least once
(real DB, real browser/CLI, real host, real local server, real cross-process boundary — whichever applies).
— the code path runs in production (e.g. a reachable Fly.io machine) and has been exercised there.
— validated by an outside party: a third-party consumer, a published benchmark, an external contributor, or a non-self deployment.
